flows.name: Discover Solo Studio on the landing page
flows.goal: Understand what Solo Studio is for and get started.
flows.outcome: Nothing is stored; after refresh the landing page still explains the workspace and how to start and share the booking page.
flows.description: A visitor arrives on the public landing page that explains the calm private workspace for clients, projects, tasks and self-serve booking, then chooses to sign in or sign up and reaches the start of the designer workspace.

flows.name: Designer sign up
flows.outcome: A designer account is created and signed in; after refresh the designer stays signed in with an empty workspace.
flows.description: A new designer creates an account with email and password from the landing page and lands in an empty workspace ready to add clients and set up booking.

flows.name: Designer sign in
flows.goal: Sign back into the private workspace.
flows.outcome: The designer is signed in; after refresh they stay signed in and see their own data.
flows.description: A returning designer signs in with email and password and returns to the home dashboard with their own clients, projects and sessions.

flows.name: View home dashboard
flows.outcome: Nothing is stored; after refresh home still shows today's sessions, this week's follow-ups and overdue tasks.
flows.description: The signed-in designer opens home to see today's sessions, follow-ups due in the next 7 days including overdue, and overdue tasks, and can jump to the related client, project or session.

flows.name: Add a client
flows.outcome: A new Client is saved defaulting to Lead when not set and is still in the list after refresh.
flows.description: The designer adds a client with name, email, optional company, profile and status, saves it, and sees it in the client list with its follow-up state.

flows.name: Track client notes and follow-ups
flows.goal: Keep notes and never miss a follow-up.
flows.outcome: Notes and follow-up dates are saved; done clears the date and push adds 7 days; after refresh the list still sorts overdue first.
flows.description: The designer browses the client list sorted overdue follow-ups first, opens a client to see dated notes, adds a note with an optional follow-up date, and marks a follow-up done or pushes it a week with one click.

flows.name: Edit a client
flows.outcome: The Client is updated and stays updated after refresh.
flows.description: The designer opens a client, changes its name, email, company, profile or status between Lead, Active and Past, saves, and sees the updated client in the list and detail.

flows.name: Delete a client
flows.goal: Remove a client and everything under it.
flows.outcome: The Client with its Projects, Tasks and Notes is gone and stays gone after refresh.
flows.description: The designer deletes a client after confirmation and returns to the client list without that client, its projects, tasks and notes.

flows.name: Add a project to a client
flows.goal: Start a piece of work for a client.
flows.outcome: A new Project linked to the Client is saved and still shows its open task count after refresh.
flows.description: The designer creates a project under a client with name, short description and optional due date and then sees it in the project list with its count of open tasks.

flows.name: Find and work through tasks
flows.outcome: Tasks are created and their Done state is saved; after refresh the project still shows the same counts, filters and highlights.
flows.description: The designer browses all projects with open task counts, opens a project to see its tasks, searches by title, filters by status and priority, adds tasks, and ticks tasks done quickly with overdue tasks standing out.

flows.name: Edit a project or task
flows.outcome: The Project or Task is updated and stays updated after refresh.
flows.description: The designer opens a project or task, changes its fields such as description, due dates, status or priority, saves, and sees the updated project and task lists.

flows.name: Delete a project or task
flows.goal: Remove work that is no longer needed.
flows.outcome: The Task is gone, or the Project with its Tasks is gone, and stays gone after refresh.
flows.description: The designer deletes a task or a project after confirmation; deleting a project also removes its tasks and the lists update accordingly.

flows.name: Set weekly availability
flows.goal: Define when sessions can be booked.
flows.outcome: Availability rules are saved; after refresh the same weekly rules are still shown and drive open slots.
flows.description: The designer sets weekly availability by adding, editing and removing weekday rules with start and end times that control which slots can be offered for the next two weeks.

flows.name: Manage session types
flows.outcome: SessionTypes are saved including the discovery, review and workshop defaults as edited; after refresh they are still shown.
flows.description: The designer reviews the pre-created session types, edits their names, durations, displayed prices and max people, and can add or remove types, seeing how each type defines slot length and fullness.

flows.name: View and cancel upcoming sessions
preconditions: Availability and session types are set.
flows.outcome: Cancelled slots and bookings are removed and freed seats reopen; after refresh the upcoming list stays without the cancelled items.
flows.description: The designer views upcoming sessions with their bookings, cancels a whole slot which removes the slot and all its bookings, or cancels a single booking to free one seat.

flows.name: Book a session from the public page
flows.goal: Book a session without an account.
preconditions: Designer has set availability and session types.
flows.outcome: A Session booking is saved and linked to the matching Client or a new Lead Client; after refresh the slot shows as booked or full and the confirmation with link is retrievable from the booking.
flows.description: A visitor without an account opens the public booking page, picks a session type, sees open slots for the next two weeks without other bookers details, books with name and email, and sees a confirmation with an on-screen cancellation link; matching email links to an existing client otherwise creates a new Lead client.

flows.name: Cancel a booking via link
flows.outcome: The Booking is removed and its seat is freed; after refresh the booking stays cancelled and the slot is open again.
flows.description: A booker opens their cancellation link without signing in, confirms cancellation, and sees that the booking is cancelled and the seat is freed.

flows.name: Designer sign out
flows.outcome: The designer is signed out; after refresh the workspace requires sign-in and the landing page is shown.
flows.description: The signed-in designer signs out and returns to the public landing page, leaving the private workspace protected until next sign-in.

fields.label: Designer email
fields.meaning: Email the designer uses to sign up and sign in

fields.label: Password
fields.meaning: Secret that proves the designer owns the account

fields.label: Client name
fields.meaning: How the designer refers to the client

fields.label: Client email
fields.meaning: Email used to match bookings to this client

fields.label: Company
fields.meaning: Optional company the client works for

fields.label: Client profile
fields.meaning: Short note about what they do, how met and what they pay
fields.example: Runs a D2C skincare brand, met at design meetup, pays per project

fields.label: Client status
fields.meaning: Where the client is in the relationship

fields.label: Note text
fields.meaning: What was discussed or decided with the client
fields.example: Call went well, wants homepage audit next week

fields.label: Follow-up date
fields.meaning: When the designer should next contact the client

fields.label: Project name
fields.meaning: How the designer refers to the work for a client

fields.label: Project description
fields.meaning: Short summary of what the project covers
fields.example: Audit and redesign of marketing homepage

fields.label: Project due date
fields.meaning: Optional date the project should be finished by

fields.label: Task title
fields.meaning: What needs to be done in the project

fields.label: Task status
fields.meaning: Where the task is in its workflow

fields.label: Task priority
fields.meaning: How urgent the task is

fields.label: Task due date
fields.meaning: Optional date the task should be done by, overdue when before today and not Done

fields.label: Availability weekday
fields.meaning: Which day of the week sessions can be offered

fields.label: Availability start time
fields.meaning: Time from which sessions can start on that weekday

fields.label: Availability end time
fields.meaning: Time by which sessions must end on that weekday

fields.label: Session type name
fields.meaning: Name of the bookable offering shown to bookers

fields.label: Session type duration
fields.meaning: Length of one slot in minutes

fields.label: Displayed price
fields.meaning: Price shown for information only, nobody pays in the app

fields.label: Max people per slot
fields.meaning: How many bookings a slot holds before it is full

fields.label: Booker name
fields.meaning: Name of the visitor booking a session

fields.label: Booker email
fields.meaning: Email used to link the booking to a client and to identify the booking

fields.label: Task search text
fields.meaning: Free text to find tasks by title

fields.label: Task status filter
fields.meaning: Show only tasks with this status

fields.label: Task priority filter
fields.meaning: Show only tasks with this priority

fields.label: Project client
fields.meaning: Which client the project belongs to

fields.label: Session type choice
fields.meaning: Which offering the booker wants to book

fields.label: Slot choice
fields.meaning: Which open time the booker reserves
